# Annotate

> Annotate is a desktop app, for people who use Claude Code on a Mac or on Ubuntu, that lets a person draw a frame around anything on their screen, type a note, and have the Claude Code chat they picked do what the note asks and say what it did. Never ask for, print or store a token or key.

## Install

It needs Claude Code (claude --version) and a Mac with Apple silicon, or Ubuntu with its standard GNOME desktop.

The person pastes one line into a terminal: curl -fsSL https://annotate.fly.dev | sh
It asks once before it installs, then offers to sign in, which can be skipped. In a Claude Code chat that was already open, the person types /reload-plugins once. On a Mac the app is Annotate in the Applications folder, so Spotlight finds it.

First-run permissions:
- macOS: when Annotate opens without a permission it needs, a window walks through each one, Screen Recording and the Microphone, with a button to its page in System Settings.
- Ubuntu: click Allow when Ubuntu asks to let Annotate take screenshots, click Add to add Annotate's keyboard shortcuts, and on the first recording pick the screen in Share Screen and click Share.

Framing needs no account. The mic and Send Feedback need the person to sign in: they choose Sign in from Annotate's menu and finish in the browser window it opens.

## Use

In a Claude Code chat, /annotate makes that chat take the frames the person sends. Claude reads the picture and the note, does what the note asks, and marks the frame done, or stuck, with one line saying what it did.

Words: a frame is the rectangle drawn over the screen; Annotate sends a picture of what is inside it with the note. The card is the small box beside the frame for the note. The inbox is Annotate's window listing each frame sent, its state (waiting for a chat, working, done, stuck) and the chat's line. Annotate's menu opens from its icon at the top right of the screen, in the menu bar (Mac) or the top bar (Ubuntu).

Commands, in the order /annotate help prints them:
- /annotate: this chat takes the frames. Annotate opens if it isn't open. Typed in another chat, the frames go there instead.
- /annotate off: this chat stops taking frames. Annotate stays open.
- /annotate open: Annotate opens. No chat takes frames until /annotate.
- /annotate quit: Annotate closes.
- /annotate where: where the frames and settings are, and where the app is.
- /annotate update (or upgrade): gets the newest version of Annotate.
- /annotate help: whether Annotate is open and which chat takes the frames, then every command and key. /annotate help more adds what leaves the computer and how to use other coding tools.
- /annotate uninstall: removes Annotate once the person says yes. See Update and uninstall.
From Annotate 1.12.12, a bare /annotate also starts and /annotate off also stops.

Keys, Mac then Ubuntu:
- ⇧⌘F, Ctrl+Shift+F: draw a frame over the screen, then type a note on its card.
- ⌘↩︎, Ctrl+Enter: send the frame and its note to the chat.
- ⇧⌘↩︎, Ctrl+Shift+Enter: record a video of the drawn frame; press again to stop. The person's voice is in the recording unless Include my voice in recordings is off.
- ⇧⌘E, Ctrl+Shift+E: show or hide the inbox.
- Esc: close the frame without sending it.

## Settings

Settings… is in Annotate's menu; on a Mac also in the Annotate menu, with ⌘,.
- Include my voice in recordings: on at first; off, recordings have no sound.
- Eyes follow the cursor: on at first. Annotate's character watches the pointer; off, it only blinks.
- Play sound effects: on at first. A short sound for each thing the person does.
- Show Annotate in the Dock (Mac): off at first.
- Start on Login: off at first.
- Menu bar icon: the character on a background, or alone.
- Microphone: which microphone the mic uses; System default unless picked.
The same switches are in Annotate's menu. Which service turns voice into words is not in the Settings window: on a Mac, hold Option (⌥) while opening Annotate's menu and pick xAI or ElevenLabs. On Ubuntu it is always xAI.

## Where your data lives

One folder holds the frames and settings; /annotate where names it.
- Mac: ~/Library/Application Support/Annotate. The app is Annotate in the Applications folder.
- Ubuntu, installed through Claude Code: ~/.local/share/annotate. The app is in ~/.claude-apps/annotate.
- Linux, run some other way (not through Claude Code): ~/.config/Annotate.
Inside it: frames.json (the inbox list), frames/ (pictures and recordings), settings.json, feedback/ (waiting until sign-in), talk-log.jsonl (how long each mic use lasted, never the words), install-id (a random number, never who the person is) and, on a Mac, annotate.log (what Annotate did, never a note). On Ubuntu installed through Claude Code that record is app.log in ~/.claude-apps/annotate. The sign-in is in the Mac's saved passwords as "Annotate desktop", or locked in the data folder on Ubuntu.

What leaves the computer:
- The chat that ran /annotate: frames, notes and recordings stay on the computer until that chat takes them; then its AI reads them like anything else in the chat (for Claude Code, they go to Anthropic with the chat).
- xAI, or ElevenLabs if picked: the voice, while the mic is on, through Annotate's server, to become text. Never frames, pictures, recordings or typed notes.
- Annotate, on Send Feedback: the note, the picture if added, and the Annotate and operating system versions. Signed out, feedback is kept on the computer until sign-in.
- annotate.fly.dev, the service that installs and updates Annotate: gives the computer an install number and sees each update download. When Claude Code opened Annotate, Annotate also sends it a short report per frame sent (how it was made: typed, spoken, drawn or recorded) and per frame done or stuck, with how long it took and a random number that is the same for every report from this computer. Never notes, pictures, recordings, name or email.

Nothing else leaves.

## Update and uninstall

Annotate checks for a newer version when a Claude Code session starts. /annotate update gets it now; it asks first, then says when to restart Claude Code.

/annotate uninstall asks "Uninstall Annotate?" (Yes goes on) and then "Also delete your frames and settings?" (No keeps them). It quits Annotate, removes the app and ~/.claude-apps/annotate, deletes the data folder only on the second Yes, and removes annotate@zaydek from Claude Code. If Annotate is still open it removes nothing and says to quit Annotate from its menu first.

Or paste this into a terminal: curl -fsSL https://annotate.fly.dev/uninstall | sh

By hand: run claude plugin uninstall annotate@zaydek in a terminal; on a Mac, drag Annotate from Applications to the Trash; delete the data folder above to remove the frames and settings.

## Works with

- Claude Code in a terminal, on macOS with Apple silicon and Ubuntu with GNOME. Tested with every release. No Intel Mac build.
- Other coding agents, such as Codex: with Annotate open, paste "Connect to Annotate at http://127.0.0.1:7420/mcp and take my frames from it." into a chat in that tool. That chat then calls annotate_start and takes frames as /annotate does in Claude Code. Best effort, not tested with each release.

## Feedback

Send Feedback… in Annotate's menu. A note, optionally a picture (Frame the screen…, or one of the person's frames), then Send. It sends Annotate the note, the picture and the Annotate and operating system versions; signed out, it is kept on the computer until sign-in.
Issues: https://github.com/zaydek/annotate/issues (public; leave out anything private).
